I-01.title: Northgate terminal: new fee for containers delivered too early
I-01.body:
From 1 December, Northgate Container Terminal will charge a daily fee on export containers that arrive more than five days before the vessel's cut-off.

The terminal says its yard has been more than 85 percent full for three weeks, as shippers deliver early ahead of the year-end rush.

The fee is billed to the shipping line, which usually passes it on to the shipper.

What to do: check the cut-off date on each booking and agree delivery dates with your trucking company so containers arrive inside the free window.

I-06.title: From booking to loading: the two cut-offs that matter
I-06.body:
Every booking confirmation lists the vessel, the voyage and two deadlines.

The container-yard cut-off is the last moment the full container can enter the terminal. The document cut-off is the last moment the shipping instructions can reach the line.

Missing either can mean missing the vessel. Most delays come from late trucks and late documents, not from the ship.

What to do: write both cut-off dates into your production plan as soon as the booking is confirmed.
